extracted.intended_audience: debt collectors, compliance officers, and federal/state regulators (entities implementing or enforcing FDCPA/CFPB rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and prohibitions (Part 1006) governing debt-collection communications, validations, prohibited practices, recordkeeping, and state-exemption procedures under the FDCPA as implemented by the CFPB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: False representation of character/amount/legal status
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not falsely represent the character, amount, or legal status of any debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits misstatements about what the debt is, how much is owed, or whether it is legally enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: False representation of services/compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not falsely represent any services rendered, or compensation that may be lawfully received, by any debt collector for the collection of a debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes misrepresenting fees, commissions, or services provided to collect the debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Threats of arrest, seizure, garnishment without lawful intent
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not represent or imply that nonpayment of any debt will result in the arrest or imprisonment of any person or the seizure, garnishment, attachment, or sale of any property or wages of any person unless such action is lawful and the debt collector or creditor intends to take such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only truthful threats of lawful actions the collector actually intends to pursue are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: False, deceptive, or misleading collection means — no threats of unlawful or unintended action
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not threaten to take any action that cannot legally be taken or that is not intended to be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad prohibition on threatening legal steps or remedies that are not available or not going to be executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: False/deceptive credit information communications
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not communicate or threaten to communicate to any person credit information that the debt collector knows or should know is false, including the failure to communicate that a disputed debt is disputed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reporting false derogatory information to consumer reporting agencies and failing to flag disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Simulated court/official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not use or distribute any written communication that simulates or that the debt collector falsely represents to be a document authorized, issued, or approved by any court, official, or agency, or that creates a false impression about its source, authorization, or approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers documents that mimic judicial or government forms to coerce payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Use of untrue business/company names
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not use any business, company, or organization name other than the true name of the debt collector's business, company, or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents anonymity via misleading business names; separate rule allows employee assumed names under conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition: False representations or deceptive means
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not use any false representation or deceptive means to collect or attempt to collect any debt or to obtain information concerning a consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all prohibition covering deceptive practices not specifically enumerated elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures required: Initial communication disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must disclose in its initial communication with a consumer that the debt collector is attempting to collect a debt and that any information obtained will be used for that purpose. If the initial communication is oral, the disclosure must be repeated in the initial written communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required wording and timing ensure the consumer knows the purpose of communication; oral-first collectors must follow up in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures required: Subsequent communications disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: In each communication with the consumer subsequent to the initial communication, the debt collector must disclose that the communication is from a debt collector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every follow-up communication must clearly identify the sender as a debt collector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures exception: Formal pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures required by initial and subsequent communication rules are not required in a formal pleading made in connection with a legal action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court filings in active litigation are exempt from the initial/subsequent communication disclosure rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated disclosures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must make the required disclosures in the same language(s) used for the rest of the communication. Any translation used must be complete and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When communicating in another language, the required disclosures must be provided in that language and must be accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed names allowance and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may use an assumed name when communicating provided the employee uses the assumed name consistently and the debt collector can readily identify any employee using an assumed name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited use of pseudonyms by collectors' employees but requires internal traceability and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair or unconscionable means prohibition (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect any debt, including the practices described in paragraphs (b) through (f) of §1006.22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General bar with enumerated examples below (collection of unauthorized amounts, postdated checks, concealment charges, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of unauthorized amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not collect any amount unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law. 'Any amount' includes interest, fee, charge, or expense incidental to the principal obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors cannot tack on unauthorized fees, interest, or charges not permitted by the contract or law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdated payment instruments rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not: (1) accept from any person a check or other payment instrument postdated by more than five days unless the person is notified in writing 10 to 3 days prior to deposit; (2) solicit postdated payment instruments to threaten or institute criminal prosecution; or (3) deposit or threaten to deposit any postdated instrument prior to the date on such instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects consumers who provide postdated checks; requires specific advance notice window if accepting checks postdated >5 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Charges resulting from concealment of purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not cause charges to be made to any person for communications by concealment of the true purpose of the communication (e.g., collect telephone calls, telegram fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors may not hide the fact a call relates to debt collection to shift communication costs to the consumer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonjudicial action regarding property restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not take or threaten to take any nonjudicial action to effect dispossession or disablement of property if: (1) there is no present right to possession through an enforceable security interest; (2) there is no present intention to take possession; or (3) the property is exempt by law from such dispossession or disablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits self-help or threats of self-help to take property where not legally or factually justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of certain media
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not: (1) communicate by postcard; (2) use any language or symbol on an envelope other than the address (except may use business name if it does not indicate debt collection); (3) email a consumer at an employer-provided address unless that address meets specified exceptions; or (4) communicate via social media if the communication is viewable by the general public or the person's contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits methods that can reveal debt to third parties or embarrass consumers; employer-provided email exceptions are narrowly defined in §1006.6(d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for certain emails/texts
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector who communicates by email or text in accordance with the procedures described in §1006.6(d)(3) does not violate the unfair/unconscionable rule by revealing the debt collector's name or other information indicating the communication relates to debt collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following §1006.6(d)(3) procedures lets collectors identify themselves in electronic messages without violating the media restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Statute of limitations and time-barred debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'statute of limitations' as the period for bringing legal action and 'time-barred debt' as a debt for which the statute of limitations has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational definitions used in the time-barred debt prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on legal actions/threats for time-barred debts
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not bring or threaten to bring a legal action against a consumer to collect a time-barred debt. This does not apply to proofs of claim in bankruptcy proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors cannot sue or threaten to sue on debts that are legally time-barred outside bankruptcy proof-of-claim contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required actions before furnishing to consumer reporting agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (a)(2), a debt collector must not furnish to a consumer reporting agency information about a debt before the collector: (i) speaks to the consumer in person or by telephone; or (ii) places a letter in the mail or sends an electronic message and waits a reasonable period to receive notice of undeliverability, monitoring for such notifications during the reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must attempt direct communication or confirm deliverability before reporting to credit bureaus; special rule for certain specialty CRAs exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sale/transfer/placement of debts known to be paid/settled/discharged
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not sell, transfer for consideration, or place for collection a debt if the debt collector knows or should know the debt has been paid or settled or discharged in bankruptcy, subject to enumerated exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include transfers to the debt's owner, prior owner where authorized, transfers due to merger/acquisition/asset transfer, secured claims in bankruptcy with transferee notice, and securitizations/pledges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment allocation for multiple debts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a consumer makes a single payment for multiple debts owed to the debt collector, the collector must not apply the payment to any debt disputed by the consumer and, if applicable, must apply the payment in accordance with the consumer's directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects consumers' direction and preserves disputed amounts from being applied improperly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional limits on legal actions by debt collectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions to enforce an interest in real property must be brought only in the judicial district where the property is located. Other legal actions must be brought only where the consumer signed the contract sued upon or resides at commencement. Nothing in this part authorizes debt collectors to bring legal actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits forum-shopping and clarifies that this part does not confer independent authority to sue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Furnishing deceptive forms
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not design, compile, and furnish any form that the collector knows would be used to cause a consumer falsely to believe that a person other than the consumer's creditor is participating in collecting or attempting to collect the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents use of forms that mislead consumers about who is involved in collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation notice timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in the exception, a debt collector must provide a consumer with the validation information required in §1006.34(c) by: (i) sending a validation notice in the manner required by §1006.42 either in the initial communication or within five days of the initial communication; or (ii) providing the validation information orally in the initial communication. Exception: not required if consumer has paid the debt prior to the five-day deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets strict timing for providing required validation information and allows oral provision if included in initial communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions related to validation notices (clear and conspicuous, initial communication, itemization date, validation period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and conspicuous means readily understandable (written/electronic must be readily noticeable/legible; oral must be at sufficient volume/speed). 'Initial communication' is the first time a collector conveys information regarding the debt (with specified exceptions). 'Itemization date' options include last statement date, charge-off date, last payment date, transaction date, or judgment date. 'Validation period' starts when validation information provided and ends 30 days after consumer receives or is assumed to receive it (assume receipt at least five days after providing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides definitions used to calculate timing and required content of validation notices and related consumer response windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation information: Required content (debt & contact details, itemization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation notice must include: the debt collector communication disclosure (per §1006.18(e)); the debt collector's name and mailing address for disputes/original-creditor requests; the consumer's name and mailing address; creditor name on itemization date if collecting consumer financial products; account number or truncated version; current creditor name; itemization date; amount of the debt on itemization date; an itemization reflecting interest, fees, payments, and credits since itemization date (may be on separate page with reference); and the current amount of the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive required fields ensure consumers can identify and verify the debt; some itemization can be provided on a separate page if properly referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation information: Consumer protections statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation notice must include statements (with the date the collector considers the validation period to end) that: (i) if consumer notifies in writing by that date that the debt is disputed, the collector must cease collection until verification or judgment is sent; (ii) if consumer requests in writing by that date the name and address of the original creditor, collector must cease collection until providing that info (if different); (iii) unless contacted by that date to dispute, collector will assume debt is valid; (iv) if collecting a consumer financial product/service, include statement directing consumer to the Bureau's website for additional information; (v) if sent electronically, explain how consumer can dispute or request original-creditor information electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include precise statements tied to the validation period and, where applicable, provide Bureau resource links and electronic dispute guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-response information format and required prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer-response information must be segregated from validation info and, if on a validation notice, located at the bottom under headings 'How do you want to respond?' and 'Check all that apply:' It must include dispute prompts with specified phrasing (e.g., 'I want to dispute the debt because I think:', 'This is not my debt.', 'The amount is wrong.', 'Other (please describe...)'), the prompt 'I want you to send me the name and address of the original creditor.' and mailing addresses for consumer and debt collector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompts must be listed in specified order and use phrasing or substantially similar phrasing; layout and segregation requirements are explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for residential mortgage debt validation
rubrics_metrics.description: For residential mortgage debt where a periodic statement is required under Regulation Z at the time of validation notice, the collector need not provide certain itemization information (c(2)(vi)-(viii)) if the collector: (i) provides a copy of the most recent periodic statement under Reg Z in the same communication; and (ii) includes on the validation notice a statement referring to that periodic statement where the omitted validation info would have appeared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows use of Reg Z periodic statements in lieu of duplicative itemization on the validation notice, with required cross-reference language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of validation information: Clear/conspicuous and Model Form B-1 safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation information must be clear and conspicuous. Model Form B-1 (appendix B) contains the required validation info and certain optional disclosures; a collector who uses Model Form B-1 complies with the information and form requirements, including if optional disclosures are omitted or certain optional disclosures added (provided optional disclosures are no more prominent). Separate page disclosures and substantially similar forms may also qualify for the safe harbor under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using Model Form B-1 (or a substantially similar form) provides a safe harbor for compliance; optional disclosures must not be more prominent than required validation info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional validation disclosures (permitted content and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collector may include optional info with validation info and receive the Model Form B-1 safe harbor if otherwise using/modifying Model Form B-1. Optional items include: telephone contact info; reference code; payment disclosures ('Contact us about your payment options.' and an 'I enclosed this amount:' prompt with payment instructions); disclosures required by applicable law placed on reverse/front per rules; electronic communications info (website, email, how to dispute electronically); Spanish-language translation prompts/phrases; merchant/affinity/facility brand; and specific info if debt is not a consumer financial product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional disclosures are allowed but must not overshadow required validation information and are subject to placement and prominence restrictions; Spanish prompts have specified Spanish-language wording options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation notices delivered electronically: formatting options
rubrics_metrics.description: If delivered electronically, prompts may be displayed as fillable fields and hyperlinks may be embedded to: (A) connect to the debt collector's website; (B) connect to the Bureau's debt collection website; or (C) permit a consumer to respond to dispute and original-creditor prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic formatting can improve interactivity but must still convey required information and preserve segregation of response prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation into other languages — rules and Spanish requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A collector may send a validation notice completely and accurately translated into any language if the collector (i) sends an English-language validation notice in the same communication or (ii) previously provided an English-language validation notice. If a collector included optional Spanish-language translation disclosures and then receives a request, the collector must provide a validation notice completely and accurately translated into Spanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits translations but requires English copy either contemporaneously or previously; if you advertise Spanish availability, you must produce a Spanish version upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Duplicative dispute; validation period (for disputes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'duplicative dispute' is a written dispute submitted within the validation period that is substantially the same as a previously submitted dispute for which the collector has already satisfied response requirements and does not include new and material information. 'Validation period' has the same meaning as in §1006.34(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the threshold for treating disputes as duplicative and the relevant time window for dispute protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on overshadowing disclosure of dispute/original-creditor rights
rubrics_metrics.description: During the validation period, a debt collector must not engage in any collection activities or communications that overshadow or are inconsistent with the disclosure of the consumer's rights to dispute the debt and to request the name and address of the original creditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must avoid communications (tone, timing, content, prominence) that would confuse or detract from the consumer's statutory dispute rights; safe harbor exists for use of Model Form B-1 as described in §1006.34(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for original-creditor information: cessation and response duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a written request for the name and address of the original creditor within the validation period, a collector must cease collection until it: (1) sends the name and address in writing or electronically in the manner required by §1006.42; or (2) reasonably determines original creditor is the same as current creditor, notifies the consumer in writing/electronically, and refers the consumer to the prior validation information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must pause collection activity while providing original-creditor details or documenting that the current creditor is the original creditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response obligations to disputes submitted within validation period
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a dispute submitted in writing within the validation period, a debt collector must cease collection of the debt or disputed portion until the collector: (i) sends a copy of verification of the debt or a judgment to the consumer in writing or electronically as required by §1006.42; or (ii) if the dispute is determined to be duplicative, either notify the consumer in writing/electronically that the dispute is duplicative and provide a brief statement of reasons and referral to earlier response, or satisfy the verification requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must stop collection activity pending verification and have specific options for handling duplicative disputes with required notices and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending required disclosures: manner and retention expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector who sends disclosures required by the Act and this part in writing or electronically must do so in a manner reasonably expected to provide actual notice, and in a form that the consumer may keep and access later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures must be delivered in a reliable, retainable way (e.g., physical mail, durable electronic format) so consumers receive and can retain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to disclosure-manner requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector need not comply with the 'reasonably expected to provide actual notice' requirement when sending the disclosure required by §1006.6(e) or §1006.18(e) in writing or electronically, unless the disclosure is included on a notice required by §1006.34(a)(1)(i) or §1006.38(c) or (d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain minimal disclosures may be treated differently unless included on specific notices triggering higher delivery standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic sending requirements: E-SIGN Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with the requirement to provide actual notice electronically for the §1006.34(a)(1)(i)(B) validation notice or the disclosures in §1006.38(c) or (d)(2)(i), a debt collector must do so in accordance with section 101(c) of the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-SIGN Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic delivery of key notices must meet E-SIGN Act standards (consumer consent, access, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must retain records that are evidence of compliance or noncompliance with the FDCPA and this part starting on the date the debt collector begins collection activity on a debt until three years after the debt collector's last collection activity on the debt (except as provided in paragraph (b) for telephone call recordings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain documentary proof of actions and decisions for at least three years after collection activity ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention special rule: telephone call recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a debt collector records telephone calls made in connection with the collection of a debt, the debt collector must retain the recording of each such telephone call for three years after the date of the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call recordings are subject to a three-year retention requirement measured from the call date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to State laws — non-preemption where state gives greater protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the Act nor this part annul, alter, affect, or exempt any person from complying with the laws of any State with respect to debt collection practices, except to the extent those laws are inconsistent with any provision of the Act; a State law is not inconsistent if the protection it affords is greater than the protection provided by the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State laws providing greater consumer protection remain effective; federal rules preempt inconsistent state laws only to the extent of inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: State exemption: ability to apply for Bureau determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State may apply to the Bureau for a determination that, under the laws of that State, any class of debt collection practices within that State is subject to requirements substantially similar to those imposed under sections 803–812 of the Act and that there is adequate provision for State enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States can seek an exemption for particular classes of practices by demonstrating substantial similarity and adequate enforcement capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural requirements (who signs and where to send)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be in writing, addressed to the Assistant Director, Office of Regulations, Division of Research, Monitoring, and Regulations, Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection, signed by the Governor, Attorney General, or State official having primary enforcement responsibility under the State law, and supported by the documents specified in the appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formal submission channels and authorized signatories for state exemption requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents for state exemption application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by: (a) a copy of the applicant State law; (b) a comparison of each federal provision with the corresponding State provision and reasons supporting the claim of substantial similarity; (c) a comparison of enforcement provisions with section 814 of the Act and reasons supporting adequacy of administrative enforcement; and (d) a statement identifying the office designated to enforce the law including facilities, personnel, funding, and enforcement procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed documentary showing of textual and enforcement equivalence is required; fiscal and personnel details should be supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria Bureau will use to determine state substantial similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau will primarily compare each provision of the applicant State law with each corresponding provision in relevant Federal law and will consider whether: (i) definitions and rules of construction import meanings and applications substantially similar to federal law; and (ii) debt collectors provide all applicable notices required by relevant Federal law with the content, terminology, form, and time periods prescribed by federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial similarity is assessed provision-by-provision (definitions, notice content/form/timelines, and enforcement provisions are central).
